name: Lanín volcano via Refugio RIM
why: A 3,776 m volcano climbed in two days: a night in a hut at the snow line, summit by dawn, the lakes of two countries below.
book: Book the ascent online on the park's system at least 72 hours ahead and register at the Río Turbio / Tromen ranger post (09:00-12:00) with the full mandatory kit: mountaineering boots, crampons, ice axe, sleeping bag. Beginners must go with an APN-licensed guide. Park entry fee. Last start from the ranger post 14:00 in summer.
water: Snowmelt near the huts only; carry a stove to melt snow and 2-3 litres for the summit day.
dangers: Ice and hard snow above the huts: crampons and an ice axe, and know how to use them.
Altitude: 2,500 m of climb from the ranger post; headache and fatigue are common.
Sudden wind and whiteouts on the summit cone.
turnaround: On summit day, turn back at the time your guide or the rangers set, summit or not: the descent takes 6-7 hours.

points.name: Tromen ranger post (Río Turbio)
points.note: By Lago Tromen on Ruta 60, near the Mamuil Malal border crossing. Kit check and registration here, then up the Río Turbio valley.

points.name: Refugio RIM
points.note: Army hut on the north face, next to the BIM and CAJA shelters. One night only; tents also allowed.

points.name: Lanín summit
points.note: 3,776 m, about 7 hours from the huts on snow and ice. Lagos Huechulafquen and Tromen below, Villarrica in Chile to the west.
